title: Listening at ballrooms; Papa Crutch and Plutsem
summary: He listened at ballroom doors, heard a boogie woogie player, was chased off pianos by Papa Crutch, and learned from the hunchback Plutsem.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well I, now remember I couldn't go in the ballrooms at this time.
You say he made piano rolls? Yeah. I didn't know that.

Yeah. That's what they told me, that he used to make piano rolls. And we used to sit on the crib and the sidewalk and look in the ballroom, you know, they had these little doors that cut from the top and bottom. And I used to listen to these piano players. Then they had a place on the wagon top where they had a wonderful Boogie Woogie piano player. We used to call him Boogie Woogie. He was a cripple fellow. And he used to play some, but that's before Boogie Woogie, I never heard any other thing about Boogie Woogie then, yeah. And I'll tell you an experience, you know, they had a lot of piano players. Everybody could play staggley or how long on the piano. And when I was learning they had a piano player by the name of Papa Crutch, he wasn't very good. Papa Crutch they used to call him. Yeah, he'd beat on the piano with his hand and everything. He was a real showman, you know. And a lot of times in these ballrooms when I would practice and he'd come in there and he'd say, get up boy, get off that piano, you don't know what you're doing. And I'd get so angry at him and I'd promise myself that someday I'd run him off a piano. And I didn't get that opportunity. You know I used to buck in New Orleans, everywhere there was musicians there would buck, you know. So you would either have to play or you'd better stay inside.
Where was it that you finally evened up the sky?

In one of the ballrooms I walked in and he was sitting down playing you know. I'd say get up man, you don't know how to play. He was so surprised. Also I had another fellow who taught me a lot on the piano. He was a very good musician but he played nice. His name was Plutsem. Plutsem? Yeah. His last name was Johnson. But we used to call him Plutsem. He was hunchback. And he taught me a whole lot on piano. Well I wish I would continue learning because now that I'm playing I'm a little handicapped in some of the things I really would like to do. I knew it but I started off with the wrong fingering of piano. And now I've got to practice and practice and practice to break the habit of playing one certain way you know.
